sources.title: Michael F. Atiyah and Raoul Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology

contents.name: Borel equivariant cohomology and coefficient-ring convention
contents.support: The Borel construction gives H_T^*(X) as the cohomology of ET×_T X and makes it a module over H_T^*(pt); the local definition matches the live batch-7 real coefficient ring and period-one character normalization.

source_review.read_extent: The definition and module structure in §2, equations (2.1)–(2.9), were inspected in full.
source_review.limitations: The paper uses complex coefficients and discusses the Cartan/de Rham model later. No Cartan comparison is used.

contents.name: Fixed-normal Euler invertibility after character localization
contents.support: The normal action has no fixed vectors; its degree-zero Euler term is a product of nonzero torus weights, while positive-degree base terms are nilpotent on a compact fixed component. This is the precise invertibility argument authored locally.

source_review.read_extent: The componentwise Euler-class argument and normal weight decomposition in §3, PDF pp. 8–9, were inspected in full.
source_review.limitations: The local proof states the character and orientation conventions directly and verifies the finite geometric-series inverse rather than relying on the source as a proof.

contents.name: Atiyah–Bott–Berline–Vergne fixed-component formula
contents.support: After localization, the restriction map is invertible; composing the fixed-component Gysin maps with inverse Euler classes and then integrating gives the fixed-component formula. The same argument yields the isolated-point specialization.

source_review.read_extent: The complete §3 proof from Theorem 3.5 through the derivation of equation (3.8), PDF pp. 7–9, was inspected.
source_review.limitations: The paper treats finite-dimensional compact manifolds with complex coefficients; its introduction explicitly says this proof does not apply directly to infinite-dimensional functional integrals. The item retains that scope boundary and uses real Borel coefficients under its exact planned real-coefficient localization input.
